subject: Sizing: NovaGen dedicated plan - memory & quant tradeoffs
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@novagen.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novagen Procurement <procurement@novagen.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing request — NovaGen long-context retrieval model

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to scope a dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for our retrieval-augmented generation product. The key constraints are: sustained 99th percentile latency <= 200ms for interactive assistants, per-request context + KV-cache up to 64k tokens for some flows, and we expect steady traffic of ~180 qps (peaks to 350 qps during business hours).

Attached is a short model profile (nova_model_profile_v2.json) and a sample prompt set. We currently run a 30B parameter model with a modest number of request-side embeddings; we are evaluating an MQA quantized variant but want to understand cost and memory implications before committing.

Questions:
- Rough GPU pool sizing (pods/gpu count) by scenario (no quant / 8-bit / mixed precision + KV offload)
- Expected latency impact when KV-cache spans GPU memory vs partial offload to host NVMe
- Any recommended canary configuration for the first 2 weeks of a reserved commitment

Can you loop in whoever should run the arithmetic? We need a short write-up to share with procurement for the reserved commitment.

Thanks,
Hannah Li
Head of Platform — NovaGen
H: +1 415-555-0182
attachments: nova_model_profile_v2.json (json), sample_prompts.txt (text)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — NovaGen long-context retrieval model

Hannah — thanks for the profile and prompts. High-level notes below; Marissa and Rishi, please add the detailed numbers / spreadsheet scenarios.

Quick answers up front:
- No-quant (FP16/AMP): baseline pod estimate ~18-22 GPUs for sustained 180 qps with 64k KV resident in GPU memory (depends on model KV density).
- 8-bit (int8) end-to-end: roughly 2.0-2.6x GPU density improvement — estimate ~8-12 GPUs, but accuracy/latency variance depends on quant approach.
- Mixed precision + selective KV offload (hot prefix on GPU, cold tails on NVMe SSD): target ~12-16 GPUs with tighter latency tail controls.

Latency notes:
- KV fully resident on GPU gives the best P99; offload to host adds ~8-25ms per token for streaming fetches depending on NVMe topology and batching. If your flows read large spans of KV per request, the_host_offload path can push P99 above 200ms unless we batch aggressively or prefetch.

Canary suggestion: Start with a 4-GPU canary running the int8 variant behind a 5% traffic route for 14 days, capture quality metrics vs ground truth, and monitor P99. If quality regression < 1.2% and P99 < 220ms under synthetic load, scale to the initial reserved pool.

I'll attach a scenario spreadsheet and ask Marissa to populate exact memory math (KV sizes by token density) and Rishi to add the quant eval summary.

— Jonas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: (will follow: kv_scenarios.pdf, quant_eval_summary.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — NovaGen long-context retrieval model

Hannah / team — I ran three capacity scenarios and summarized them in the attached PDF (kv_scenarios.pdf). Highlights:

Scenario A — FP16 resident KV (no quant):
- KV per token: 96 bytes (model-specific KV packing for 30B)
- Average live prefix per request: 18k tokens -> ~1.7 GB per concurrent session for KV alone
- Pod sizing: assume 40% headroom -> 20 GPUs for 180 sustained qps; peak safety to 350 qps -> 30 GPUs for buffer

Scenario B — End-to-end int8 (aggressive quant):
- KV per token reduced to ~36 bytes; model params compressed similarly
- Effective GPU capacity improves ~2.7x; estimate 9 GPUs for baseline, 15 for peak safety
- Caveat: int8 LL quantization increases risk on rare-case generation; recommend prompt-level QA gating

Scenario C — Mixed precision + KV tiering (recommended):
- Keep model state in FP16 for head layers, int8 for less-sensitive layers; KV stored hot on GPU for last 8-12k tokens, older KV tiered to NVMe SSD with prefetching
- Pod sizing: 13 GPUs baseline, 20 GPUs for peak safety; gives ~1.4x cost improvement versus FP16 while keeping P99 within target with proper batching and prefetch windows

Operational items for procurement packet:
- Canary config (4 gpus int8) + evaluation metrics to gate rollback
- SLA target (P99 <= 200ms) with an agreed degradation window during weekly rollouts
- Durable KV retention policy (TTL) and recommended autoscale headroom

Attaching kv_scenarios.pdf with the underlying math and a per-GPU memory table.

— Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: kv_scenarios.pdf (PDF)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — NovaGen long-context retrieval model

Adding the quant evaluation results. TL;DR: per-prompt ROUGE/QA metrics show an average relative degradation of 0.9% with post-training 8-bit quant (layerwise per-channel), but there are tails (up to 3% worse) on prompts with heavy numeric reasoning or long-chain grounding. Mixed-precision (FP16 for first 6 transformer blocks + int8 for remainder) reduces the tail to ~1.1% and retains ~1.6x memory improvement vs FP16.

Notes for the pool:
- If Novagen requires strict correctness for certain flows (billing, legal responses), we recommend pinning those flows to FP16 sub-pools or routing via a higher-accuracy model variant.
- We ran evals on eval://runs/quant-eval-20280321 — full CSV attached (quant_eval_summary.csv).

Happy to run any additional prompt-slices you want; I can prioritize numeric reasoning and retrieval-heavy prompts.

— Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
